decisions.summary: FreeGround built once per stage: static surely-taken cells where the site boundary is installed (empty otherwise, stated) plus the placed boxes at the 2 px margin, added as each bundle lands (D7 grid); asked first for every spiral offset and every _slide step (dispersed); on the nucleated path it answers _envelope_blocked placed-box hits in list order and prunes static ground only where the loop judges ground (union envelope; a side box only when the union was refused; a moved box at its moved position); same-seat tests on both paths including the union-clear, side-sample-on-taken-ground case
decisions.why: Unchanged since the third plan review (CLEAR); its ruling carries: Both round-2 rulings resolved, checked against the code. (1) The index is now the one FR-003 and the approved analysis name: built once per stage (install_site_boundary runs once, stages.py 130) and updated as each bundle lands through the placed registry index, which follows the Indexed list across the _solve_homestead rebind. Dispersed drops are exact: a house-rect sample point in a surely-taken cell is refused by _site_blocks_rect (the house conjunct of _bundle_common_fits), and a placed-box overlap at the margin is _bundle_side_fits refusal (fit.py 463, strict, +2), both conjuncts of the order-independent _bundle_fits; the slides are covered, since _slide ends on a _bundle_fits NO (place.py 81) and grove_off_field does not touch either conjunct. The no-boundary case is stated: only the placed boxes answer, which is the part that grows with density (the request stated purpose, the city). (2) The nucleated branch now matches place.py 146-174: the union is asked first (a taken sample point makes _union_clear False, exactly as _rect_blocked would), a side box is judged only when the union was refused (line 152), ground-refused returns True before any placed-box move so a static drop never pre-empts a move, and a single placed overlap stays a move with list order kept. The index prunes, the exact test decides. Summary C, research R2 and the Constitution Check now say the same thing.

decisions.summary: dispersed pre-screen of every spiral candidate and slide step: before the bundle is built, the house rect's static ground, the house within the placed-box margin and the eave gap (_seat_refused); once moved from its template, every part's static ground, bbox vs canvas margin and bounding ring, bbox within the placed-box margin, and the three sun rules (_bundle_refused); not on the nucleated path
decisions.why: The extension checked against the code, conjunct by conjunct. _seat_refused: geom['house'] is exactly (x, y, hw, hh) (template house at the origin, moved, and _rake_parts carries only yard, gardens and kura); the static test is FreeGround's surely-taken cells at the nine points _site_blocks_rect asks; the placed-box test on the house implies the side fit's refusal because the dispersed bbox (grove frame west..east, north..south, plus yard and garden) holds the house; the eave gap is _house_too_near_a_neighbor on the same rect. _bundle_refused: FreeGround exists only while _site_chains is installed (set together in install_site_boundary, cleared together at stages.py 558-560), and then _rect_blocked returns _site_blocks_rect whatever fields says, so testing the groves and the yard/shed/gardens by the same nine points is exact; the canvas margin, the bounding ring and the placed-box comparison are _bundle_side_fits' own lines; _sun_corridor_ok, _gardens_sun_ok and _yard_sun_conflict are conjuncts of _bundle_common_fits/_bundle_side_fits (the yard-is-None guard only prunes less). Every one is a conjunct of the order-independent _bundle_fits, so the pre-screen prunes and the whole test decides, as FR-003 and the approved analysis ask; the slide still stops at the first refusal. The nucleated path is untouched (no call from _place_bundle_nucleated), so round 1's D9b ruling holds. test_the_free_ground_changes_no_seat disables all three pre-screens and asserts identical seats, both forms, both scenarios - enforcement of FR-003's 'no loss of fidelity', not scope.
